EventService/HandleEvent.payment_succeeded: the global scenario asserts a top-level `event_status` field, but `EventServiceHandleResponse` (proto/events.proto) has no such field - it carries event_type, event_content, source_verified, merchant_event_id, event_ack_response and supported_integrity_checks and nothing else - so this assertion cannot pass for ANY connector. Same finding adyen records for its own HandleEvent scenarios. The fixture in webhook_payload.json is real and was verified end-to-end by hand against EventService/HandleEvent (sourceVerified=true, eventType=PAYMENT_INTENT_SUCCESS, status=CHARGED); it goes live the moment the global scenario or its assertion is fixed.

EventService/HandleEvent.refund_succeeded: Braintree emits no refund-success webhook at all. `refund_failed` is the ONLY refund kind on the Braintree webhook surface - there is no `refund_settled` and no `refund_succeeded` - so a successful refund is observable only through RefundService/Get (RSync). The global scenario asserts event_type WEBHOOK_REFUND_SUCCESS, which this connector can never produce.
